tonight.headline: 0-3, and Achane is still in your lineup
body: Week 4 hasn't started. ESPN has you at 114.1 against Aye-Aye's 125.3 and a 45% chance, but that counts Achane's zero in an RB slot. Starting Tuten takes the lineup to 126.9, level with them.
Two things before Wednesday 01:00 Mexico City: move Tuten into Achane's slot, and make sure the Gordon claim is in. After that, Friday's injury report decides Jefferson, Coker and Allen.

case.label: The swing
case.body: Tuten's 12.7 for Achane's 0.0 is worth more than any other decision this week. The rest of the lineup already matches the projection.

case.label: The risk
case.body: Three starters are QUESTIONABLE: Allen (knee contusion), Jefferson (ankle sprain) and Coker (quad strain). Every report says all three could play, but you have no QB behind Allen, and your two WR fallbacks lock before Sunday's inactives.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Friday's final report. An OUT or DOUBTFUL on Jefferson means starting McLaurin before 07:30 Sunday. On Allen, it means a free-agent QB add.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sun 11:00 (Tuten's kickoff) — do it now
doFirst.title: Start Tuten in Achane's RB slot
doFirst.subtitle: Achane is out for the season and is still in your starting lineup. That's 12.7 projected points for one tap.

case.label: The trigger
case.body: This is last week's ghost card firing. Achane tore his ACL (CBS citing ESPN and NFL Media, 28 Sep) and he's on IR in the league file, still in slot 2.

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: Jacksonville's lead back: 15, 13, 15 carries, 60–65% of the backfield, and 15-73-1 in Week 3 (NBC). He projects 12.7, ahead of Kamara (10.6) and Monangai (9.0) by more than the two-point coin-flip line.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Kamara or Monangai outscores Tuten in Week 4. Graded on the archive's result.

doFirst.title: Claim Ollie Gordon II, drop Achane
doFirst.subtitle: Carried from last night and still right. AVIATO is now 1st in waiver order, so if this claim is in, it wins.

case.label: The role
case.body: Gordon took all the RB work after Achane went down: 17 carries, a goal-line TD and three catches (NFL.com, 28 Sep). The archive has him at 14.5 points. Hafley expects him and Wright to form the core of the backfield (Yahoo).

case.label: The drop
case.body: Achane is 96.8% rostered, so this goes against the market on the record, for one reason: he's out for the season and Chem has no IR slot. He holds a roster spot and can't score.

case.label: The contested part
case.body: SI and The Big Lead prefer Jaylen Wright; DraftKings and NFL.com rank Gordon ahead. Wright is 'day-to-day' with a stinger and foot injury, the same label that kept him out of Week 3 (RotoWire, 28 Sep), and he's OUT in the file. I take Gordon: he's healthy and he has the job now.

case.label: The priority
case.body: Chem's order resets weekly and AVIATO is first in this snapshot, so the claim costs nothing lasting. ESPN doesn't show rival claims, so check the claim is actually submitted.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Wright returns and Gordon draws under 12 touches in Week 4, which would make it a timeshare. Or Monangai outscores Gordon in two of Weeks 4–6.

doFirst.subtitle: The fallback the tool printed can't wait for Sunday's inactives. McLaurin kicks off in London at 07:30, five hours before Jefferson's 12:35 check.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Right-ankle sprain; Rapoport says it isn't anything long-term and Jefferson could play against Miami (NBC, 28 Sep 19:31 ET; ESPN). Wednesday to Friday practice decides.

case.label: The timing problem
case.body: lineup_check.py names McLaurin as the fallback at 12:35 Sunday, but Washington play Indianapolis in London at 07:30. By Jefferson's inactives McLaurin is locked. Boston plays Thursday. So the WR decision has to be made on Friday's report.

case.label: If he's questionable and sits
case.body: At 12:35, move Coker from FLEX to WR and put Kamara (Monday night) in the FLEX. Kamara is the only bench player still unlocked by then.

case.label: Why McLaurin
case.body: Nine targets in each of the last two weeks, 41% of Washington's in Week 3. Mariota likely starts again: Daniels travels with a dislocated elbow but may sit (CBS, 28 Sep).

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The card fires and Jefferson plays after all. Or it fires and McLaurin is outscored by the player he replaced.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Left-knee contusion from a hit while running in Week 3. Brady isn't concerned, and Dr. David Chao calls him 'hurt, not injured' and expects him to face New England (SI, 28 Sep).

case.label: Why Murray
case.body: He's the Vikings' starter, and Minnesota traded J.J. McCarthy to the Giants on 28 Sep (NBC; ESPN), so the job is his. He projects 19.5 and is on waivers until Wed 01:00, then free if nobody claims him. Mariota (18.6) is second, but Daniels may return in London.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Monangai: ten carries, no targets in Week 3, fifth back once Tuten starts.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Allen is active Sunday, and the card never fires. That's the expected outcome.

action.label: Add Murray · drop Monangai (only if Allen is out)

whatWentWrong.title: Lost 103.8 to 140.6, with 34.1 left on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: The best lineup from this roster scored 137.9 and still lost by 2.7. The biggest single gap was Coker over McLaurin, a brief's call: 3.8 against 19.7.

case.label: The archive
case.body: Started 103.8. Best available 137.9: Tuten (17.0) for Achane (1.7), McLaurin (19.7) for Jefferson (5.2), Boston (8.1) for Coker (3.8). Achane and Jefferson were injury exits, so those two swaps can't be graded as lineup errors.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing about the method. The projection chose Coker by 1.9, a coin flip, and the brief wrote a thesis on it anyway. That thesis is closed WRONG. This week's flex has no thesis.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A lineup call this week that departs from the projection without unpriced news. None is proposed.

whatWentWrong.title: Both WR fallbacks lock before Sunday's inactives
whatWentWrong.lead: Boston plays Thursday and McLaurin at 07:30 in London. Jefferson's inactives come at 12:35 and Coker's at 16:50.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: The lineup tool prints McLaurin and Boston as fallbacks without checking their own kickoffs. Following it on Sunday means finding both already locked.

case.label: The fix
case.body: Decide Jefferson on Friday's report (card above). Kamara, on Monday night, is the only late fallback.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Both receivers practise fully by Friday, and none of this is needed.

worthALook.name: Braelon Allen
worthALook.lead: The Jets' lead back while Breece Hall is out. For now, a coin flip with Tuten, not a card.

case.label: The role
case.body: Hall is week-to-week with a quad injury and won't play Chicago (Last Word on Sports, 29 Sep; Rapoport). Allen and Isaiah Davis share the work; Davis hasn't played an offensive snap yet (RotoWire, 28 Sep).

case.label: The number
case.body: He projects 13.0 against Tuten's 12.7. That's a 0.3 gap, a coin flip. He also has no seat: Achane's goes to Gordon, who holds the job for the rest of the season, while Allen's lasts until Hall returns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Hall is ruled out beyond Week 4 and a second seat opens, e.g. Allen (QB) is healthy and Monangai becomes expendable. Then Allen over Monangai is worth a claim, since Chem priority resets.
